handbookNote: Michigan Real Estate Broker (and Associate Broker -- same single exam qualifies a candidate for either arrangement, directly analogous to how the pa_re_broker/ny_re_broker banks treat their own states' associate-broker concepts) license exam. Vendor: PSI Services LLC under contract with the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA). Exam mechanics CONFIRMED directly from PSI's official Michigan Candidate Information Bulletin (Copyright 2024, updated 10/8/2024, fetched and read in full from https://test-takers.psiexams.com/mire's linked PDF): the Broker exam is a SINGLE combined exam of 115 scored questions (worth up to 120 total points, since national broker-exam scenario-based questions can be worth up to 2 points each -- this bank tracks a simplified 115-question/75%-correct model since the practice-exam format cannot replicate PSI's partial-credit scenario scoring), 75% passing (raw passing score 90 out of 120 points on the real exam), 210 minutes, examination fee $79. A small number (5-10) of unscored experimental/pretest questions may also appear. The bulletin's own content outline splits the exam into two parts sharing the same 115-question pool: a National (Real Estate Principles and Practices) portion covering 11 weighted topic areas (Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19%, Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5%, Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12%, Real Estate Calculations 6% -- summing to 100% of ~75 national items), and a Michigan Specific Portion covering 5 areas with explicit BROKER item counts (Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board 3 items, Licensing Requirements 4 items, Statutory Requirements Governing Activities of Licensees 15 items, Contractual Relationships 5 items, Additional State Topics 13 items -- summing to 40 state-specific items, i.e. 115-75=40, consistent with the bulletin's separate item-count table). This bank's 16-bucket structure maps directly onto these same 16 official outline sections (11 national + 5 Michigan-specific) rather than an invented taxonomy, since the outline itself is the authoritative source for what's tested and in what proportion. Licensure prerequisites (broker/associate broker): CONFIRMED via direct research into MCL 339.2504 (90 hours of approved pre-licensure education, including at least 9 hours of civil rights law and equal opportunity in housing; must be completed within 36 months of application unless the applicant held an active salesperson license during that period) and MCL 339.2505 (3 years' equivalent full-time experience in the business of real estate, with Mich. Admin. Code R 339.22217 defining acceptable related experience) -- bucket agents for the Licensing Requirements and Statutory Requirements buckets should independently re-verify these and the minimum age via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov rather than treating this note as the final word. Real citations available from the PSI bulletin's own 'Examination Study Materials' reference list (all independently fetchable from legislature.mi.gov and michigan.gov/orr) include: OCCUPATIONAL CODE (1980 PA 299) Articles 1-6 (MCL 339.101-339.606) and Article 25 (MCL 339.2501-339.2518, the core real estate broker/salesperson licensing article); MICHIGAN ADMINISTRATIVE CODE, Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons -- General Rules (R 339.22101-339.22667); MICHIGAN ADMINISTRATIVE CODE, Occupational Boards -- Part 7 Disciplinary Proceedings (R 339.1701-339.1771); OCCUPATIONAL LICENSE FOR FORMER OFFENDERS (1974 PA 381, MCL 338.41-338.47); SELLER DISCLOSURE ACT (1993 PA 92, MCL 565.951-565.966); PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES CIVIL RIGHTS ACT (1976 PA 220, Article 1 MCL 37.1101-37.1103, Article 5 MCL 37.1501-37.1509); ELLIOTT-LARSEN CIVIL RIGHTS ACT (1976 PA 453, Article 1 MCL 37.2101-37.2103, Article 5 MCL 37.2501-37.2507, Article 6 MCL 37.2601-37.2606, Article 7 MCL 37.2701-37.2705, Article 8 MCL 37.2801-37.2804); LAND DIVISION ACT (1967 PA 288, MCL 560.261, the Public Act 591 private-road disclosure); LANDLORD AND TENANT RELATIONSHIPS (1972 PA 348, MCL 554.601-554.616); TRUTH IN RENTING ACT (1978 PA 454, MCL 554.631-554.641); CRIMINAL USURY (1968 PA 259, MCL 438.41-438.42); REAL ESTATE TRANSFER TAX (1966 PA 134, MCL 207.501-207.513) and STATE REAL ESTATE TRANSFER TAX ACT (1993 PA 330, MCL 207.521-207.537); MICHIGAN CONDOMINIUM ACT (1978 PA 59, MCL 559.101-559.276); STATE HOUSING DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT (1966 PA 346, MCL 125.1401-125.1499c); MICHIGAN ANTITRUST REFORM ACT (1984 PA 274, MCL 445.771-445.788); NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION ACT excerpts (1994 PA 451, Part 21 Subparts 4/8/11, MCL 324.2109 et seq.); MICHIGAN RIGHT TO FARM ACT excerpt (1981 PA 93, MCL 286.473c, seller's-disclosure trigger); RECORDING AFFIDAVITS AFFECTING REAL PROPERTY (1915 PA 123, MCL 565.451-565.453). This is a BRAND-NEW state build (not a backfill) -- mi_re_salesperson already exists separately (118 questions, untouched by this build) and is a genuinely distinct exam (Salesperson: 115 questions, 70% passing/80 raw points, 180 minutes, ~80 national+35 state-specific items) confirmed via the same PSI bulletin. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate track rate. Answer choices should be drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout by every bucket agent, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via a rotation script after all buckets are built, matching every other broker track in this project.
